newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve double pricing for goods.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve double pricing for goods.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Tuesday an EU directive which will force shops to indicate the price of goods both by item and by weight.
This will mean, for example, that a packet of cheddar cheese will be labelled to show the price of the cheese in the packet and the price of a kilo of cheddar.
For six months before and after the introduction of the European single currency, labels will also show the price of the item in both national currencies and euros.
Catering establishments, hospitals, vending machines and itinerant traders will not have to comply with the new rules.
Euro-MPs called for 20 amendments to the draft directive -- COM(95)276 -- even though these were rejected by the Council of Ministers when it adopted its common position on the text.
One of the most important amendments concerned the arrangements for small retailers.
Parliament said small retailers should have six years to adapt to the new rules, by which time the European Commission should have produced clear details of how much it will cost.
The Council favours excluding small retailers from the directive altogether.
The proposal needs the support of both ministers and Euro-MPs to become law.
